title: Condensed Matter Phase Transition Barriers with Known K

systems.name: BKT 2D XY vortex core
systems.notes: Core energy of a vortex in 2D XY model = pi*J. Well-established.

systems.name: 4He superfluid film (BKT)
systems.K_source: Superfluid order parameter psi = |psi|*exp(i*phi) — 2 real DOF
systems.reference: Bishop & Reppy, PRL 40, 1727 (1978); Nelson & Kosterlitz, PRL 39, 1201 (1977)
systems.notes: Universal BKT vortex core energy = pi * k_B * T_BKT

systems.name: Josephson junction array (BKT)
systems.K_source: U(1) phase variable — 2 real DOF (cos phi, sin phi)
systems.reference: Resnick et al., PRL 47, 1542 (1981); Newrock et al., Solid State Phys. 54, 263 (2000)
systems.notes: Electrically measured vortex core energy. Matches 2D XY universality.

systems.name: 1D Ising domain wall
systems.notes: Exact: domain wall costs 2J. Lowest barrier in Ising hierarchy.

systems.name: 2D Ising interface tension (T=0)
systems.reference: Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944); Peierls, Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 32, 477 (1936)
systems.notes: Interface tension sigma(T=0) = 2J. Exact. NOT the nucleation barrier (which depends on field).

systems.name: 3D Ising interface tension (T=0)
systems.notes: T=0 interface tension. All Ising models give sigma(T=0)=2J regardless of dimension.

systems.name: VO2 metal-insulator (Peierls)
systems.K_source: One d_parallel orbital per V-V dimer pair (Goodenough 1971)
systems.reference: Berglund & Guggenheim, Phys. Rev. 185, 1022 (1969); Goodenough, J. Solid State Chem. 3, 490 (1971)
systems.notes: Quasi-1D Peierls instability. E_a from Arrhenius fit of resistance switching.

systems.name: SrTiO3 cubic-tetragonal AFD
systems.K_source: TiO6 octahedral rotation: 3 Euler angles (Glazer tilt system)
systems.reference: Salje et al., J. Phys.: CM 10, 5535 (1998); Muller & Burkard, PRB 19, 3593 (1979)
systems.notes: E_a from twin domain wall motion. Three rotation DOFs for the AFD order parameter.

systems.name: BaTiO3 ferroelectric switching
systems.K_source: Polarization vector P=(Px,Py,Pz) — 3 components from cubic parent
systems.reference: Merz, Phys. Rev. 95, 690 (1954); Miller & Weinreich, Phys. Rev. 117, 1460 (1960)
systems.notes: Switching barrier from Arrhenius fit. DFT intrinsic barrier is lower (24 meV).

systems.name: YBCO vortex creep barrier
systems.K_source: Vortex center-of-mass position in ab-plane: 2 coordinates
systems.reference: Maley et al., PRB 42, 2639 (1990); Blatter et al., RMP 66, 1125 (1994)
systems.notes: Single-vortex creep regime. U_0 varies 500-2000K depending on field/T. Using lower bound.

systems.name: NbSe2 vortex creep barrier
systems.K_source: Pancake vortex position in ab-plane: 2 coordinates
systems.notes: Single vortex creep. Layered 2H polytype. Varies significantly with field.

systems.name: CuMn spin glass (elementary)
systems.reference: Chamberlin et al., PRB 26, 5352 (1982); Fisher & Huse, PRB 38, 386 (1988)
systems.notes: Elementary (single-cluster) barrier. Aging barriers are much larger and grow with time.

systems.name: Transverse-field Ising 1D (Gamma=0)
systems.K_source: Spin has s^z and s^x active: 2 quantum DOF
systems.notes: Exact 1D. At Gamma=0 recovers classical 1D Ising. Barrier interpolates to 0 at QCP.

systems.name: CeRhIn5 AFM spin gap
systems.K_source: Three major Fermi surface sheets from dHvA (Shishido et al. 2005)
systems.reference: Hegger et al., PRL 84, 4986 (2000); Shishido et al., JPSJ 74, 1103 (2005)
systems.notes: Spin gap from resistivity. K from independent dHvA measurement.

systems.name: BCS superconductor gap (s-wave)
systems.K_source: Complex order parameter psi = |psi|*exp(i*phi): 2 real DOF
systems.reference: BCS, Phys. Rev. 108, 1175 (1957). Ratio confirmed in Al, Sn, Pb, In, Nb, etc.
systems.notes: Universal weak-coupling BCS result. 2*Delta/(k_BT_c) = 3.527. Strong-coupling corrections exist.

KC-1.description: At least 8/15 systems with B/d within 15% of pi/sqrt(2)

KC-3.description: Cross-system R^2 for B vs d > 0.9

KC-4.description: f(K) = B/(d*B_G) is monotonic in K

verdict: Framework barrier universality does NOT transfer to condensed matter energy barriers. Different universality classes give different B/d ratios. This delineates a scope boundary: the framework operates on Fisher information manifolds (behavioral probability spaces), not physical energy manifolds.
